thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Firm as Apple Leads Tech Stocks Higher; Street Looks Ahead to Fed Policy Announcement

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Firm as Apple Leads Tech Stocks Higher; Street Looks Ahead to Fed Policy Announcement
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Wednesday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +0.7%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.5%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): +0.4%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.4%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 1%.
US stock futures were gapping higher ahead of the open, boosted by upbea t earnings results from Apple (AAPL), Boeing (BA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD).
Investors are also looking ahead to the conclusion of the Federal Reserve's two-day policy-setting meeting later Wednesday. Chairman Jerome Powell is expected to hold a news conference to discuss the central bank's plans at 2:30 p.m. ET.
Concerns over the US-China trade talks may weigh on market sentiment, however, especially after the US filed criminal charges against Chinese company Huawei of stealing trade secrets and violating sanctions imposed on Iran.
In economic data news, ADP reported the US economy created 213,000 private-sector jobs in January, versus forecasts for 174,000 jobs. ADP also lowered its initial estimate of new jobs in December to 263,000 from 271,000.
Still ahead, data on pending home sales in December will be released at 10 am ET.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 1.4% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were flat.
Apple (AAPL) rose nearly 6% after the company reported late Tuesday Q1 EPS of $4.18, up from $3.89 a year earlier, just ahead of analysts' estimates of $4.17 in a Capital IQ poll. Revenue fell 5% to $84.3 billion from the year-ago quarter, but still ahead of the $84 billion estimate. Revenue from iPhone declined 15% from the prior year, while total revenue from all other products and services grew 19%. For fiscal Q2 2019, Apple expects revenue of $55 billion and $59 billion, against the Street consensus of $59 billion.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.4% in the pre-market session. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 1.3% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X Shares (FAZ) was down 1.6%.
Blackrock (BLK) rose more than 1% after the firm said it has slashed its holdings in Danske Bank to 4.99%, which is below the just below the 5% threshold where it is obliged to inform the market. Danske Bank is at the center of money laundering investigations after suspiciously moving payments worth EUR200 billion ($228.66 billion) through its Estonian operations between 2007 and 2015. The lender is under investigation in Denmark, Britain, Estonia and the US.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) and other funds iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), and Vanguard Industrials (VIS) were quiet in pre-market trading .
Boeing (BA) rose nearly 6% after the aircraft manufacturer posted Q4 adjusted earnings of $5.48 per share, up from $5.07 in the same period a year ago and topping the estimate of $4.55 from analysts polled by Capital IQ. Total revenue of $28.34 billion was up from $24.77 billion in the same period a year ago and topped the Street projection of $26.76 billion. Boeing said it expects full-year 2019 adjusted EPS in the range of $19.90 to $20.10, exceeding the Street estimate of $18.41. The company guided 2019 revenue in the range of $109.50 billion to $111.50 billion, topping the Street projection of $106.72 billion.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.5% in pre-market trade.
Cloud Peak Energy Inc (CLD) fell 2% after the company said it hired Centerview Partners LLC as its investment banker, Vinson & Elkins LLP as its legal advisor, and FTI Consulting, Inc. (FCN) as its financial advisor to help review its capital structure and restructuring alternatives. Its Board approved an updated executive retention program for the senior management team, which replaces the previously announced November 2018 retention program.
Commodities
Crude was up 1%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 1.3%. Natural gas was down 1.3% while the United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.4%.
Gold was up 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was was up 0.1%. Silver was up 0.4%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.4%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were inactive.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were quiet in pre-market trade.
Tupperware Brands (TUP) fell more than 8% after the firm reported Q4 adjusted earnings of $1.33 per share, down from $1.59 in the same period a year ago and in line with the estimate of $1.33 from analysts polled by Capital IQ. Total revenue of $505.9 million was down from $588.6 million in the same period a year ago and missed the Street projection of $550.5 million. Tupperware expects Q1 2019 adjusted EPS in the range of $0.90 to $0.95, below to in line with the Street projection of $0.95. The company expects Q1 sales to be down 8% to 10% from $542.6 million in Q1 2018. The guidance implies a range of $488.3 million to $499.2 million, missing the Street projection of $512.4 million. The company expects full year 2019 adjusted EPS in the range of $4.06 to $4.21, missing the Street estimate of $4.45. It expects full year sales to be down 2% to 4% from $2.07 billion in 2018. The guidance implies a range of $1.99 billion to $2.03 billion, missing the Street projection of $2.08 billion. The company said it is cutting its quarterly dividend to $0.27, from $0.68 in the prior quarter.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.01% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were flat in pre-market trade. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 0.1%.
Can-Fite Biopharma (CANF) jumped 14% after the company said Drug Design, Development and Therapy published an article presenting data from numerous studies showing adenosine's role in inhibiting inflammatory cytokine production. Can-Fite's Piclidenoson, a Phase III drug candidate, and Namodenson, a Phase II drug candidate, both target the A3 adenosine receptor (A3AR), which the company says it believes may treat cytokine release syndrome (CRS) while also promoting an anti-cancer effect.
